title: Matrix-Free Finite Volume Kernels on a Dataflow Architecture
problem: Solving large and complex linear systems from Finite Volume discretization of PDEs for geological carbon storage is computationally and memory expensive due to severe memory latency and bandwidth bottlenecks that dominate simulation time.
motivation: Safe long-term geological CO2 containment is critical for climate change mitigation strategies.
method: The approach solves large systems of equations that come from Finite Volume discretization (a technique that approximates physics equations by dividing space into small volumes). Instead of computing and storing a complete matrix (a large grid of numbers), the algorithm computes only what it needs on-the-fly, which saves memory. It runs on a dataflow architecture—specialized hardware designed to pass data directly between calculations without going through slow main memory—which keeps data access fast and eliminates the memory delays that normally dominate simulation time.
key_novelty: Matrix-free Finite Volume kernels (computing results on-the-fly rather than storing a matrix) on dataflow architecture (specialized hardware for efficient data routing) overcome memory bottlenecks in large geological simulations.
contributions: Matrix-free algorithm tailored for Finite Volume-based linear systems
Dataflow architecture implementation minimizing memory latency and bandwidth bottlenecks
Two orders of magnitude speedup compared to GPGPU implementations
1.2 PFlops peak performance on a single dataflow device
